> Some osteophytes and irregular thining of intra-articular cartilage of left knee, reflecting osteoarthritis
  Wearing of articular cartilage and tiny subchondral cyst over patellar ridge, reflecting grade 3-4 chondromalacia (Srs/Img: [ID].
> Patellar enthesophyte; tendinosis of quadriceps tendon and iliotibial band.
> Mild fat stranding over suprapatellar fat pad, R/O suprapatellar fat pad impingement syndrome
> Joint effusion and suprapatellar bursitis with suprapatellar and medial plicae; hypertrophy of the synovium, indicative of synovitis.
  Lobulated hyperintensity foci with internal septums in retrocondylar region of left knee, reflecting retrocondylar bursitis/ gastrocnemius bursitis.
  Small Baker's cyst and popliteus bursitis.
> Linear signal intensity in posterior horn of medial meniscus, without significant extending into the surface, in favor of grade 2 intrasubstance signal of posterior horn of medial meniscus, maybe due to degeneration or meniscal vascularity. 
> Mild interstitial increased signal intensity of ACL on F/S T2WI, in favor of degeneration.
> PCL, medial & lateral collateral ligaments appear to be within normal.
> Subcutaneous infiltration over left anterior knee.

Impression: 
1. Osteoarthritis of left knee, more prominent at patellofemoral joint with focal grade 3-4 chondromalacia. 
2. Mild synovitis of left knee with patellar plicae and small Baker's cyst and retrocondylar bursitis/ gastrocnemius bursitis. (Srs/Img: [ID]; 6/9-14)
4. Grade 2 intrasubstance signal of posterior horn of medial meniscus, maybe due to degeneration or meniscal vascularity.
5. Mild subcutaneous edema over left anterior knee.
6. Suprapatellar fat pad impingement syndrome and tendinosis of quadriceps tendon.
7. Degeneration of ACL.
Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation and physical examination

Right knee MRI without contrast:

INDICATION: Rule out right knee meniscal tear.

COMPARISON: No prior for comparison.

FINDINGS:

No significant effusion. No loose body.

Anterior compartment:
Overall mildly chondrosis with small fissures on the lateral and medial facets of the patella less than 50% of the thickness. Area of subchondral sclerosis on the lateral facet. Patellar and quadriceps tendons intact. Retinacula are intact. Hoffa fat pad unremarkable.

Medial compartment:
Mild chondrosis. Presence of a small meniscal flounce in the anterior body of medial meniscus without definitive tear. Capsular meniscal interface intact. Medial collateral ligament intact. Pes anserine unremarkable. Moderate insertional tendinopathy within the semimembranosus tendon.

Lateral compartment:
Mild chondrosis no significant meniscal tear. Lateral collateral ligament intact. Biceps femoris tendon intact. Iliotibial band intact. Popliteus tendon is intact.

Intercondylar compartment:
Mild cystic changes within the tibial eminence and mild high signal intensity within the anterior cruciate ligament and could be in keeping with intraligamentous beginning degenerative mucoid changes. Posterior cruciate ligament intact.

Multiple varicose veins on the medial aspect of the knee in the subcutaneous tissues.

CONCLUSION:
1. Mild to moderate patellofemoral chondrosis.
2. Semimembranosus insertional tendinosis without tear. No discrete ligament or meniscal tear identified.
3. Multiple varicose veins to the medial aspect of the knee in the subcutaneous tissue.

Control de lesión condral de la faceta lateral de la rótula derecha. Colitis. Se cuenta con
resonancia previa para comparar del [DATE].

MRI RIGHT KNEE:

INDICATION:    assess mpfl tear, osteochondral fragment   .

PRIOR IMAGING:    
.
TECHNICAL INFORMATION AND PROTOCOL:

Proton density and T2 weighted sagittal, coronal and axial imaging was performed through the knee including a 3D Fat suppressed proton density weighted sequence. No contrast was administered.

FINDINGS:

The 3-D proton density sequence was reformatted and manipulated to aid in the interpretation of this examination.

The patella is laterally subluxed and there is diffuse edema seen along the course of the medial patellofemoral ligament consistent with a high-grade injury. This extends to the femoral attachment and also involves the attachment at the patella. The lateral patellar retinaculum is intact and appears unremarkable.

There is intraosseous edema within the medial patella and contour flattening of the medial surface of the patella. There is associated edema in the lateral femoral condyle consistent associated with the osteochondral impaction along the lateral cortical surface in keeping with transient lateral dislocation of the patella associated with osteochondral impaction of the medial surface of the patella and lateral femoral condyle.

The quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact.

There is trochlea dysplasia and lateralization of the tibial tubercle with the TT-TG distance measuring 2.1 cm. Articular cartilage of the patella demonstrates focal fraying at the patellar apex. The trochlear surface is reasonably well-maintained.

The lateral meniscus is intact. The articular cartilage of the lateral joint compartment appears to be well maintained.

The medial meniscus is intact. The articular cartilage of the medial joint compartment is well-maintained.

The anterior cruciate ligament is intact and appears unremarkable.

There is mild intrinsic signal within the posterior cruciate ligament but intact fibers are present and the signal changes may in part be artifactual.

There is edema around the proximal and mid fibers of the medial collateral ligament consistent with low-grade medial collateral ligament sprain.

The lateral collateral ligament complex including fibular collateral ligament, biceps femoris tendon, popliteus tendon and IT band all appear intact and unremarkable.

There is a small to moderate knee effusion. There is no Baker's cyst demonstrated.

INTERPRETATION: 

Torn medial patellofemoral ligament associated with bone contusions an osteochondral fracturing of the medial surface of patella and lateral femoral condyle associated with transient dislocation of the patellofemoral joint.

Moderate chondromalacia patella.

Background changes of lateralization of the tibial tubercle and shallowness of the trochlear groove predisposing to patellar dislocation.

Low-grade medial collateral ligament tear.

Nonspecific signal in the posterior cruciate ligament favored to be artifactual.

Zentrierte Stellung im rechten Kniegelenk. Zentrierte Stellung der Patella. Keine trochleäre Dysplasie. Regelrechter Knorpelbelag retropatellar. Gering streifige hypointense Signalveränderungen des Knorpelbelages zentral in der Trochlea mit subchondral kleinzystischen Veränderungen und Ödemsignal, hier V.a. fokal osteochondrale Läsion (5/15, 4/19 + 6/20). Keine wesentliche Chondropathie femoro-tibial im medialen und lateralen Kompartiment oder retropatellar. Keine wesentliche Gelenkspaltverschmälerung. Kleine umschrieben T2-hyperintense Läsion in der Femurmetaphyse mit 7 mm (5/19, 4/14), morph. passend zu einem Enchondrom. Gering Gelenkerguss, keine freienn Gelenkkörper. Intaktes vorderes und hinteres Kreuzband. Intaktes mediales und laterales Kollateralband. Unauffällige Darstellung des medialen und lateralen Meniskus bezogen auf Formgebung und Signalintensität. Intakte Darstellung der Quadriceps- und Patellarsehne. Unauffällige Darstellung der umgebenden Muskulatur und Weichteile.
